notes: The San Francisco City Planning Commission's minutes of its regular and special meetings, January to June 1975, from the one volume the San Francisco Public Library contributed to the Internet Archive for that year (30minutesofsanfran1975sa; the July-December 1975 volume, which would be number 31, is not in the collection). Pages were split from the hOCR search text on the Internet Archive page index, counting the viewer page among the leaves scandata.xml does not mark addToAccessFormats=false. Every page is dated from the meeting header it sits under. Four kinds of finding: what the Commission decided about a property, dated to the meeting that decided it; what the minutes state stood on or occupied the property; dated past facts the minutes state about a building; and landmark designations. A proposal on its own is not a finding. A Board of Supervisors action the minutes report without its own date is framed 'by' the date of the meeting that reported it. The minutes name applicants, owners, attorneys, objectors, commissioners and staff throughout; the reader spec (in research/sources/sf-planning-commission-minutes.md, under Reader spec) barred all of them from every field, and kept companies, institutions, named buildings and architects.

coverage.remaining: Every page of the 1975 volume (30minutesofsanfran1975sa, January-June 1975) was read; the July-December 1975 volume is not in the collection (the identifier sequence skips 31). Volumes 32-39 (1976-1980) and 40-58 (1994-2005) remain. Of the 39 unresolved, 26 print no street number (the Victoria Mews and Mira Glen developments, the Golden Gate Heights blocks, the Nihonmachi bowling-alley lot on Webster, the Pacific Rendering site on Jennings, the One Market Plaza garage at Howard and Steuart, the Jefferson Street bakery, the Daly City BART lot on Belle Avenue, the Rickard Street freeway land, Lotta's Fountain, Sutro Heights, the Muni Metro Center, the Redding School, the Christian school on Whittier, Howard and Main, and Lot 22 of Block 68 on Hyde, re-lotted); 8 have no EAS record at the number (1919 California, 4136 Third, 849 Niagara, 2106 24th Street, 445 Harney Way); 4 are condominiums waiting on #446 (101 States, 676 Capp); 1 names Edgar Place where EAS holds only an Edgar Avenue.
coverage.note: 350 OCR pages with text out of 714 viewer pages (716 scanned leaves), read in one session by a single reader from the dossier's Reader spec; 23 meetings (22 regular, 1 special) from 9 January to 26 June 1975, each dated from its own header. 102 findings: 53 decisions, 37 statements of what stood on a property, 7 landmark designations or Board landmark actions, 5 dated past facts. Every quote was re-anchored mechanically against its own page (102 of 102). 63 resolved: 53 by the EAS join on a printed number, 10 by hand on a named building the site already carries (the Atherton House, the Goodman Building, Children's Hospital, the Bank of Tokyo building at 350 California, the old Federal Building at 50 United Nations Plaza, the Southeast plant at 750 Phelps, the Opera House twice, the Mills Tower at 220 Bush); one EAS join (20 Edgar Place onto EDGAR AVE) taken back to unresolved. 61 published on 40 pages, 18 of them seeded; 2 declined as already on the page. One conflict recorded: 361 Oak Street dated 1868 by the owner's representative against the roll's 1885 (building.completed_conflict and unknowns). The half-year's distinctive matters: the Board of Supervisors overriding the Commission on the Atherton House and Goodman Building landmarks and a Bryant Street wrecking yard; the Nihonmachi bowling-alley rezoning carried 4-2 over about 70 objectors; the Capp and Bartlett rezoning to R-3; and the Pets Unlimited soundproofing dispute at 2343 Fillmore, closed 4-3 in June.
